purpose: Gate A/B/C/D regression and validation cases for the Stage9 analytic-geometry diffuse-interface wetting boundary condition. Plane cases verify the analytic path does not break the previously-passing flat-wall result. Cylinder and sphere cases verify the analytic path fixes the curved-wall wetting failure that stages 5-8 could not resolve.
build_variant_required: d3q27_pf_velocity_q27_geometric (OPTIONS_q27=on, OPTIONS_geometric=on). AnalyticWetting=1 requires the geometric build so gradPhiVal_* fields are available.

cases.name: plane_theta030
cases.purpose: Flat-wall regression: analytic path must match legacy flat-wall theta030 to within fitting noise.

cases.name: cylinder_theta030
cases.purpose: Curved-wall wetting gate D. Verifies the analytic normal (radial in the y-z plane) fixes the curved-wall wetting response.

cases.name: sphere_theta030
cases.purpose: THE CASE THAT WAS FAILING IN STAGES 5-8. Originally fitted ~107 deg for a 30 deg target (sign reversal from lattice-normal quantisation). The analytic radial normal must recover the wetting response. Gate B = 1000-step smoke; gate C = 200000-step long.

honest_caveats: Stage9 is exploratory_not_validation until a separate read-only audit accepts the gate results.

The analytic wetting BC requires a lattice solid mask for the analytic surface (cylinder/sphere) so bounce-back still works. The case XML declares the analytic geometry via Model params; the user must still supply the solid mask through TCLB's standard geometry tool or an STL.

The diffuse-interface BC has O(W/R_drop) sharp-interface approximation error. For R_drop=24 lu and W=6 lu this is ~25% on the leading tan term; the curvature correction absorbs the O(h^2/R) wall-geometry error (~1% for R=24, h=0.5).
Gate E (dynamic plane impact) is not included in this case set; it is a post-validation extension that reuses the same BC.

The first-iteration gradient reads PhaseF=-999 on wall nodes before calcWallPhase writes the mirrored fluid value. This is one iteration of gradient noise and is inherited from upstream TCLB; it does not affect the steady-state result.
